## Failure paths and arms (fill in)

All final acceptance arms below used the unchanged candidate above. Raw stdout/stderr,
controller fault scripts and per-row NDJSON remain in the private local artifact root
`/home/kjelly/.cache/go-build/issue211-scratch/` (mode 0700). The table binds the
principal artifacts by SHA-256; it does not imply they are published with this record.

- Baseline `613c3616`: the real engine generated a fresh rule-5710 JSON alert, but
  the TCP-only receiver received none; csyslogd reported 5302 while manager verify
  incorrectly passed 11/11. Baseline receiver checks C7/C8 failed because that initial
  setup omitted its local audit-forwarding prerequisite; no baseline whole-chain PASS.
- Stock Ubuntu TCP supplemental chain: 23 PASS, zero failures/skips, both hosts
  `changed=0`. Source-scoped receiver TCP/514 DROP: fresh engine alert generated,
  local C11 matcher PASS, delivery FAIL (rc1). Exact rule removed in `finally`;
  a newly generated challenge delivered PASS. Stopping rsyslog alone was an invalid
  earlier fault because socket activation restarted it; that attempt is not denial proof.
- Legacy managed UDP block migration via `--tags C11` removed the old block and
  recreated the manager. A second C11 apply reported `changed=0`. Real engine stopped,
  both current and daily hardlinks renamed, then engine restarted: a distinct new
  inode was syslog-readable and its fresh alert arrived. Renaming only the current
  hardlink on an earlier candidate was invalid rotation proof and is not counted.
- Real engine future-year test: only the owned manager guest clock advanced to
  2027-01-02, creating a new year/month and new daily inode; read access and fresh
  delivery passed. Guest UTC and original NTP service were restored in `finally`;
  another fresh delivery passed. Controller/receiver clocks were never changed.
- Exact frozen helper harness ran on the manager VM with real POSIX ACLs: all
  13 arms passed, including reader effective rights, restrictive masks, concurrent
  parent/child creation, descriptor-bound replacement, symlink/FIFO refusal and
  identity-aware rollback of JSON/text/checksum/archive siblings without deleting data.
- Full manager role post-ACL failure: a temporary one-shot validator shim delegated
  to the real binary until the ACL grant, created four new regular output siblings,
  then intentionally returned rc98. Actual C11 apply returned rc2/rescued=1;
  exact prior year ACL, preserved bytes, revoked inherited reader ACLs, clean journal
  and active rsyslog were independently checked. Owned shim/flags were removed.
  The first immediate fixture failed rc2: its input at 05:44:43 preceded collector
  startup at 05:44:46. This failure is retained. A later new fixture and receiver
  NDJSON passed; it does not establish delivery of the first nonce.
- Receiver TCP/22 collision: actual apply failed rc2/rescued=1; prior configuration
  SHA-256 and active service restored, then a newly generated alert delivered PASS.
- Optional forwarding disable via C11 removed the reader, disabled its profile,
  retained all three Wazuh containers and generated a new local alert successfully.
- RELP/mTLS on the same candidate: 23 PASS and both `changed=0`, using matching
  rsyslog/rsyslog-relp `8.2610.0-0adiscon1noble1` from the publisher's signed Ubuntu
  v8-stable repository, installed only by external test preparation. Stock 8.2312
  correctly failed the existing required-capability gate; it was not bypassed.
  Receiver denied the manager certificate SAN: local C11 PASS but fresh delivery
  FAIL; restoring authorization allowed a new delivery. TCP/514 stayed loopback-only.
  Co-located manager/receiver/audit roles also passed all 23 checks and idempotency;
  Wazuh and auth message counts stayed exactly one after the observation interval.
- The primary machine record is the final **stock, fresh `--ephemeral`** run with
  normal cluster snapshot/rollback enabled, independent of all preceding fault state.
  It passed syntax, fresh check-mode, apply, all 23 checks and both-host `changed=0`;
  both owned VMs were automatically destroyed after success.

## Not covered / limits (fill in)

This proves the tested Ubuntu 24.04/Wazuh 4.14.1 topology and explicitly constructed
faults, not every platform, natural midnight event, outage duration or queue capacity.
Forced hardlink replacement and a real future guest clock are distinct from waiting
for a natural production rotation. No production systems or unrelated VMs were changed.
The failed-apply recovery listener can precede logcollector readiness: an immediate
diagnostic may fail closed and requires a new fixture after service startup. No
successful verdict is inferred from configuration checks or a previous nonce.

RELP results require the tested newer publisher runtime; production playbooks do not
silently add that repository. Existing unknown/classic queue migration was rejected
as designed; no queue state was forcibly converted. Shared dev-lite Harbor seeding
returned HTTP401, so these runs intentionally used the committed uncached topology;
no cache credential reset was performed. TLS fixtures are synthetic and private;
no key material or private vars file is published. Machine redaction covered the
values known to its invocation; the separate publication scan covers the three known
test keys and private-key blocks, not all possible secrets.
